If you do re-enter, stop-limits (not plain stops) are non-negotiable at this valuation level; a market this stretched corrects fast when it turns.

The FDA's Advisory Committee voted 3–9 against efficacy in July (non-binding), and the FDA's final call is due today; outcome not yet known as of this report. This is closure/context only — binary-catalyst trading is still paused per the Jul 27 pivot, so no re-entry regardless of what the FDA decides today.

📚 Today you learned

Complete Response Letter (CRL) & Resubmission Classes

A CRL is the FDA saying "not yet" on a BLA/NDA — it's not a rejection, it's a formal list of what has to change before approval. What happens next depends on the resubmission class: a Class 1 resubmission (minor fixes — labeling, manufacturing data) gets a 2-month review clock; a Class 2 (new clinical data, like a fresh trial readout) gets 6 months. CAPR's deramiocel took the Class 2 path — the original CRL got lifted in March after they resubmitted with HOPE-3 Phase 3 data, which is what set today's Aug 22 PDUFA date. An Advisory Committee vote along the way (CAPR's went 3-9 against efficacy in July) is non-binding — the FDA can and does override AdCom votes in both directions, which is exactly why the outcome today is genuinely uncertain, not a formality.

Also today: Complete Response Letter itself — the FDA's non-approval letter that starts the resubmission clock in the first place.
